Days/week and split type come from your Training Plan settings (Settings tab).
Fixes every exercise to the same set count; left on "let AI decide", it varies by exercise.
?
Pinning it is applied on the way in as well as asked for in the prompt, so the plan gets the number you chose whatever the model returns. With a session length set, fixing sets means the AI adjusts the number of exercises to fit instead.
Kept between generations — saved automatically as you leave the field, so clear it once it no longer applies.
Uses your OpenRouter API key from Settings, calling OpenRouter directly — nothing passes through any server of mine.
Units
Only changes how weights are entered and displayed — everything is stored in kg internally, and switching never touches logged history.
Lifter profile
Pick the one matching what's actually happening now, not how long you've trained — this app also detects it per-lift from your logged history.
?
The standard definition of these levels is how long you need to recover enough to add load — session, week, or block — and calendar time is only a rough proxy for it: novice progression typically runs 3–9 months but people burn through it anywhere from 8 weeks to well over a year. It's also per-lift, not global — most people are still novices on overhead press long after their squat isn't.
Used only as AI plan-generation context — it deliberately does not change how fast weight is added.
?
Meta-analysis of controlled trials finds women's relative strength gains equal to men's in the lower body and slightly greater in the upper body. What differs is absolute load, and the load-relative increments elsewhere in this form already account for that without needing to know your sex.
Applies a small taper to the progression rate past 40 — a judgment call, not a number lifted from a study.
Used to compute the real load on bodyweight/assisted exercises — a +10 pull-up isn't a 10 lift without knowing what it's added to.
In a deficit, holding load is a good result — progression slows, so repeating last week's numbers counts as a win, not a miss.
Workout
2–3 min suits heavy compounds; 60–90s is plenty for isolation work — it doesn't run after an exercise's last set.
On by default — turned off, logging a set just records it, with no countdown or sheet.
On by default — asks once per exercise, right after its last prescribed set; skipping is one tap and changes nothing.
Set per equipment type — a barbell, dumbbell rack and pin stack all move in different-size steps, and this sets the floor on how finely load can advance.
?
The jump is a property of the implement, not of you: a barbell with 1.25kg plates moves in 2.5kg steps, a dumbbell rack in 2kg or 5lb steps whatever you'd prefer, and a pin stack in 5kg steps regardless. On light lifts, this floor overrides your experience setting entirely. Each exercise picks up a type automatically from its name; correct any of them on the Exercises tab.
OpenRouter
No key stored yet — paste one above; it saves automatically, unencrypted, so use a spend-limited key.
Check openrouter.ai/models for current options and pricing — not hardcoded here since it goes stale.
?
Prefer a fast instruct model over a reasoning model. This task fills in a fixed JSON shape from a supplied list, which isn't what extended thinking is for: reasoning models bill their thinking as output tokens, take far longer, and some finish a long think without ever emitting an answer. If a reasoning model is the one you want, that works — the status log below reports reasoning separately from the answer, so you can see which one you're waiting on.
Training Plan
Presets are just shorthand for a sentence added to the AI prompt — anything you can describe in words works as well.
Written straight into the prompt in place of a preset — left blank, the AI picks the structure itself.
Import Data
Merge is right for a first import; Replace re-imports a file you've already loaded without duplicating sets.
?
Replace clears the existing sets of the exercises the file covers, for each day, before writing — so nothing doubles up. Sets you logged in-app for exercises the file doesn't mention are left alone either way.
Backup & restore
Downloads a single .json file with every workout, exercise, preference, plan and setting — your OpenRouter API key is deliberately left out, so it's safe for cloud storage or email.
There is no password reset. If this passphrase is lost, the encrypted file can never be opened again — by you or anyone else. The plain export above never carries this risk.
Restore replaces everything on this device — for a new phone or a wipe recovery, not for merging two devices.
This backup is encrypted. Enter its passphrase to continue — there is no way to recover it or preview the file without one.
Deletes every logged workout only — catalog, preferences, plans and settings survive — and cannot be undone.
